request.spec:
A steward can delegate the steward role to a user for a from-date and a to-date, inclusive, by the
sheet's today (a form; DELEGATED user=<user> from=<date> to=<date>; anyone but a steward, or a
to-date before the from-date, is refused with an error on the form). While the sheet's today is
inside the range the user acts as a steward in every rule; every audit line of a change that user
makes then (not the ROLLUP and TOTALS lines, nor a later line that only reports figures, such as
ALERT) ends with for=<the steward who delegated>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can delegate the steward role to a user for a from-date and a to-date, inclusive, by the
sheet's today (a form; DELEGATED user=<user> from=<date> to=<date>; anyone but a steward, or a
to-date before the from-date, is refused with an error on the form). While the sheet's today is
inside the range the user acts as a steward in every rule; every audit line of a change that user
makes then (not the ROLLUP and TOTALS lines, nor a later line that only reports figures, such as
ALERT) ends with for=<the steward who delegated>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added delegation of the steward role, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests. Because the test accepts audit lines that have extra fields on the end, I also read the audit file directly. `for=vic` appears only on wes's two changes made while today was inside the range. Wes's later lines (dated 2026-03-13) and the ROLLUP/TOTALS lines don't have it.

**How it works**
- **Storage:** a new migration (`V41__delegation.sql`) adds a delegations table. Each row holds the user, the steward who delegated, and the from and to dates.
- **Endpoints:** `GET` and `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/delegations`. A successful delegation writes `DELEGATED sheet=… by=… user=… from=… to=…`.
  - Viewers are turned away first, as on every other change.
  - Only someone whose own assigned role is steward can delegate, so a delegated user can't pass the role on. The test checks this: wes is refused while acting as steward.
  - A to-date before the from-date is refused.
  - A blank from-date means the sheet's today; a blank to-date means the same day as the from-date.
- **Acting as steward:** `RoleRepository.roleOf`, which every role rule already calls, now returns steward while the sheet's today is inside one of the user's delegations. A new `assignedRoleOf` gives the role without delegations, and only the delegate check uses it.
- **`for=` on audit lines:** this is done in one place, `Audit.record`. It reads the sheet and user from the start of each line and adds `for=<steward who delegated>` when a delegation covers today. ROLLUP, TOTALS and ALERT lines never get it. If two delegations cover the same day, the latest one names the steward.
- **Screen:** a new Delegations section (`features/delegation/`) has the form (`delegate-user`, `delegate-from`, `delegate-to`, `delegate-submit`, `delegate-error`) and lists each delegation made as a `delegate-line`.

**Choices you may want to change**
- **NOTIFY lines** (watcher notices from a change) do get `for=`, because they aren't figures. If you count them as report-only, add `"NOTIFY"` to the excluded set in `Audit.java`.
- **Long user names:** the user is read from the text after `by=` up to the next ` key=` field. A user name that itself contains something like ` x=` would be read wrongly.
- **The steward who delegated** isn't checked again later: a delegation keeps working even if their steward role is taken away afterwards.
